changes_made.explanation: Normalized dataset name to standard capitalization. Expanded models list to include all major models mentioned in evaluations. Added True/False output type which is used in CulturalBench-Hard evaluation.
Normalized metric name to standard capitalization. Only accuracy is used as the evaluation metric throughout the paper.

Removed GPT-4o and 'classification prompt' as these were used for topic classification during dataset creation, not for evaluating generated outputs. The paper does not use LLMs as judges to evaluate model outputs.

guideline: Annotators were instructed to brainstorm culturally relevant scenarios based on their personal experiences and verify questions with multiple selection settings

changes_made.explanation: Removed all items as they relate to dataset creation and annotation, not to evaluation of generated outputs. The paper does not conduct human evaluations of the LM outputs - only uses human annotations for creating and verifying the benchmark questions.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on creating a cultural knowledge benchmark (CulturalBench) and evaluating language models' performance on it. The human involvement was for dataset creation/verification, not for evaluating model outputs. The evaluation is purely automated using accuracy metrics. The paper evaluates 29 models across two settings: multiple-choice (CulturalBench-Easy) and True/False (CulturalBench-Hard).
